snapshot.name: oce
snapshot.guidance: This is an isolated OCE integration candidate. Keep all source PR heads, bases, states and auto-merge settings unchanged. Keep fork main and codex/raw-integration unchanged. Never publish releases, tags, images or deployments. The engine alone may retain objects and publish its candidate. Keep the latest upstream improvements. Preserve all published migration SQL bytes and journal entries from the previous integration; append required evolution. Source PR16 and PR19 are closed and supplied by upstream; do not reintroduce their obsolete partial implementations. Follow the target repository instructions. No dependency installation or reconciliation as a verification side effect; use the configured local audits and hosted CI for missing dependencies. npm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false for all pnpm invocations. Generic feature defects and their exact upstream-facing fixes must be identified separately from combination adaptations. No source-PR writes are authorized.

features.intent: Support trusted custom Installation profiles, explicit Preset seeding, and readable custom starters.
Grant exact Agent access to every accepted Configuration Secret through the regular save workflow.
Preserve native plugin permission and admission across Harness selection and changes.
Give each person an exact configured native OpenClaw role, independent from OCE administration, with admission and revocation.
Prepare native administration on first Agent deployment while keeping exact runtime access authority.
Manage revision-owned Gateway HTTPS egress with exact per-Agent policy, lifecycle withdrawal, and immutable admission.
Support Microsoft Teams alongside Slack, including editor, directory, exact callback ownership and guarded native media.
Support the explicitly enabled embedded Slack and Teams trial using the managed channel-derived outbound path.

adapters.guidance: Preserve exact per-person configured role and Agent use authority alongside first-deployment preparation and upstream assigning-session protection. Administration alone must not grant runtime use.

Aggregate Slack and Teams gateway/control-plane requirements through the generic revision-owned managed proxy. Retain native media URL, redirect, token and TLS guards. Do not restore the retired shared Slack proxy, legacy proxy URLs or installation-wide Teams host lists. User proxy/trust-marker overrides are reserved; dedicated Harnesses receive neither Gateway credentials nor its trust marker.

Support both Slack and Teams in embedded and dedicated modes. Embedded trial defaults off, uses runtime.channels.experimentalEmbeddedChannels, requires managed outbound and only channel-derived destinations. Additional approved hosts remain dedicated-only. Preserve callback exact owner/revision/UID/resourceVersion fencing, serving annotation authority, provider cutovers and full cleanup.

Render trusted embedded opt-in only in the existing nested runtime.channels.experimentalEmbeddedChannels. Retain paired API/worker checksums and shared-credentials warning; opt-in requires enabled managed outbound.

or shared ancestry does not establish semantic equivalence. Identify remaining
behavior, upstream replacements and consequential compatibility concerns. Cite
concrete source paths/commits/tests in evidence. Propose dependency/order changes
with reasons; do not modify source or configuration. Use needs_decision when
intent conflicts with upstream rather than silently choosing new behavior.

configuration, or weaken validation. The engine owns Git and runs the configured
checks. If the job requires a design decision, report needs_decision with evidence.

prompt_texts.repair:
# Exact candidate repair

Read the exact failed leaf logs and receipts in the recorded check state. Diagnose
product, invalid composed fixture, infrastructure and missing credentials separately.
Only candidate fixes are authorized. Preserve main, published integration and all
feature PRs. Generic feature bugs need an upstream-facing finding in the report;
do not silently label them integration problems. Preserve the published migration
prefix and all required proof. If target test code or CI suite registration is
wrong, repair its supported setup and add/extend meaningful regression coverage.
Do not change the frozen control recipe, hide skips, weaken sandboxing or install
local dependencies. Do not rerun a whole workflow merely to erase a failure.
prompt_texts.refresh:
# Independent upstream contribution

Refresh only this feature against the exact frozen upstream. Preserve its source
history and useful intent; remove superseded behavior when upstream already owns
it. This does not authorize feature branch publication. Do not import private
integration compatibility into this feature. Actual new or changed behavior needs
meaningful owning regression coverage and repository-required suite registration.
Use repository testing instructions. Missing local dependency graphs are an honest
verification limit, never authorization to install or fake them. The configured
source audit is structural only; combined hosted CI supplies broader proof later.
prompt_texts.order:
# OCE ordering

Inspect interfaces, lifecycle ownership and exact refreshed code. Previous OCE
composition used profiles, secrets, plugins, roles, first-admin, outbound, teams,
embedded; that is historical evidence, not a prescribed stack or constraint.
Prefer upstream foundations before consumers when the actual code supports it.
An integration adaptation is not automatically an upstream source dependency.
No feature PR or its base may change. Propose only justified relationships.
prompt_texts.assess:
# Assess within the authorized integration intent

Determine whether each feature remains useful against the frozen upstream. Report
concrete generic regressions separately from combined adaptations. A regression
that unequivocally contradicts an existing upstream-supported workflow is ordinary
refresh work: preserve upstream behavior in the local candidate, extend its owning
regression test, and leave the original PR untouched. Do not propose intentionally
narrowing upstream Configuration-save behavior; that is outside this assignment.

In particular, retain shared channel/Secret reference validation and accepted bound
reference forms. Resolve provider deployment prerequisites at the existing admitted
runtime boundary without globally replacing Configuration-save rules. Reassess this
from actual selected code rather than treating this instruction as proof of a bug.

Managed outbound, Teams callbacks and embedded provider compatibility are already
authorized composition work described by the recipe adapters. Independently useful
source features must not be restacked. Distinguish a mandatory source dependency
from a combination adaptation or preferred composition order. Ask for a decision
only when intent cannot be resolved from the stated requirements and current code;
never manufacture replacement work for a feature actually absorbed upstream.

report.summary: The embedded Slack/Teams trial remains useful and is not absorbed by frozen upstream. Integration requires a Configuration-save regression repair and the authorized outbound, provider, and callback adaptations. No intent decision is needed. Assessment only; no files, Git state, or remote resources changed.
evidence: Remaining feature: at 94346f810, apps/controller/src/drivers/compute/kubernetes/configuration-rules.ts::requireChannelTopology and index.ts add trusted experimentalEmbeddedChannels admission, embedded provisioning, and revision-time checks. At upstream 8e20e2019, requireChannelTopology still rejects embedded channels and agentProvisioning advertises only dedicated execution. Upstream therefore does not supply equivalent behavior.

Generic refresh regression: 94346f810 index.ts::validateConfigurationContent unconditionally calls requireTeamsConfiguration, including when the trial is disabled. That function requires explicit appId/tenantId UUIDs and an object-shaped appPassword environment reference. Upstream tests/integration/configuration-controller.test.mjs:2197–2334 explicitly accepts saving bound Teams password strings without those deployment prerequisites, including ${MSTEAMS_APP_PASSWORD} and $MSTEAMS_APP_PASSWORD, and accepts corresponding Preset defaults. Applying the trial validator unchanged contradicts that supported workflow.

Upstream replacement to preserve: c40b22b6f introduced packages/occ/src/channel-secret-bindings.ts and shared Configuration-save/deployment validation; 56af0a512 expanded runtime reference-form coverage. Frozen upstream checks embedded references, fallback expressions, shorthand secret inputs, and unreadable Slack token objects. The feature head's private collectChannelSecretBindingIds recognizes fewer forms and must not replace this shared implementation.

Outbound composition mismatch: selected outbound a50b14647 replaces runtime.channels.proxyUrl transport with immutable revision.gatewayOutbound snapshots. index.ts::admitGatewayOutbound currently refuses nonempty requirements for embedded execution. The embedded feature instead uses runtime.channels.proxyUrl/managedProxy and the shared slack-proxy.mjs. Thus the requested managed channel-derived path needs an adapter; neither source independently implements the combined behavior.

Provider compatibility concern: embedded index.ts applies HTTPS_PROXY and NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY to the combined Gateway/model process, with NO_PROXY limited to local/service destinations. Its slack-proxy.mjs allows Slack and optionally five Microsoft hosts, excluding model endpoints. Outbound a50b14647 similarly supplies only internal bypass hosts in gatewayOutboundTransport. Preserving native model execution therefore requires the authorized provider adaptation; channel-only proxy acceptance does not prove model connectivity.

Teams composition overlap: embedded index.ts::reconcileTeamsCallback and Teams head 93c1dc4f2 both manage the same Agent callback resource names and public listener. Embedded adds a revision-selecting callback Service and NetworkPolicy; Teams derives callback ownership from the serving Deployment and supplies directory/editor/media support. These are overlapping implementations to reconcile, not evidence that either feature requires restacking on the other.

Consequential upstream changes must survive: 774b3d676 introduced discoverable Driver configuration validation; 908ffe5be enforces Gateway tool policy at save and for embedded Agents; 854b1ddf5 centralizes runtime source metadata. Frozen upstream deploy/runtime/openclaw-source.json pins 554f0b886bde6c089578c49967227f8b50d1cf16. Port the opt-in and Teams packaging onto these current owners rather than restoring the older constructor, validation, or runtime-image implementation.

Verification performed: node scripts/ci/run-tests.mjs audit passed at 94346f8101230627f206ed9731f2c32beba27bad, with 391 discovered files, 391 selected files, and no issues. No installed node_modules graph exists in this checkout. Runtime, browser, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, and hosted CI results were not established in this assessment; no dependencies were installed.

Existing behavioral proof: tests/conformance/kubernetes-compute.test.mjs covers trusted opt-in/default refusal and callback candidate fencing. tests/integration/kubernetes-compute-provisioning-real.test.mjs contains the regular API/PostgreSQL/Kubernetes scenario covering exact Secret projection, revision replacement, Teams disable/reenable, and stop after disabling the option. Its comments explicitly exclude native Teams dispatch, JWT verification, public TLS, and model execution. Historical passes in the implementation plan do not qualify the frozen-upstream combination.
The embedded feature changes no migration files relative to a7aa9219f. It provides no reason to alter previously published migration SQL or journal entries.
suggestions: Generic refresh repair: remove provider deployment prerequisites from unconditional Configuration-save validation. Preserve upstream shared channel/Secret validation and accepted bound forms. Resolve and validate Teams prerequisites at the existing runtime admission boundary, repeated during preparation as appropriate. Extend the owning configuration-controller regression case without weakening its existing acceptance assertions; leave the source PR untouched.

Combination adaptation: retain the trusted default-off embedded flag, allow its channel-derived requirements through managed outbound admission, and preserve immutable snapshots, exact Agent/revision ownership, withdrawal, and default denial. Replace the trial's shared proxy wiring with the selected managed path. Handle admitted native model connectivity explicitly without globally broadening channel destinations or narrowing Configuration save.

Combination adaptation: consolidate Teams callbacks into one serving-revision-owned lifecycle, retaining exact POST routing, identity-header removal, native JWT delegation, candidate isolation, and stop/disable cleanup. Preserve Teams directory/editor/media behavior and add msteams packaging to the current upstream runtime build.

Qualification: retain current upstream CI lanes and runtime pin. Run the owning Configuration regression, Compute conformance, profile/Helm checks, and existing real API/PostgreSQL/Kubernetes workflow after adaptation. Qualify fresh-image Teams loading and managed provider connectivity separately; fixture lifecycle success cannot establish those outcomes.

order_suggestions.reason: Prefer establishing managed outbound before applying the embedded compatibility adapter. This orders local composition, not source branches: the embedded source is independently useful, but the requested combination must replace its legacy shared-proxy transport.
evidence: a50b14647 apps/controller/src/drivers/compute/kubernetes/index.ts::admitGatewayOutbound rejects embedded requirements.
94346f810 index.ts uses runtime.channels.proxyUrl and managedProxy for embedded channel transport.

order_suggestions.reason: Prefer establishing the shared Teams callback/package behavior before applying the embedded exception, then reconcile their overlapping callback ownership. This is a composition preference, not a mandatory source dependency or restack.
evidence: 93c1dc4f2 and 94346f810 both modify the same msteams callback names, Helm listener, and runtime plugin packaging.
94346f810 supplies its own Teams prerequisites, so it does not require the Teams source branch as an ancestor.

report.summary: First-admin remains useful and is not absorbed by frozen upstream. Retain its deployment-time preparation, preserve upstream improvements, and adapt it to the selected per-person roles feature. No intent decision or mandatory source dependency was identified. No files or remote state were changed.
evidence: At 37fac70dfb784351544189ad07909588b327ef47, packages/occ/src/index.ts calls optional Compute.configureAgent with the allocated Agent during deployment admission. Kubernetes native-admin.ts prepares the exact origin and device approval while preserving opt-outs and rejecting conflicts. API composition, worker.ts, worker.mjs, Helm and Compose supply matching origin inputs.

At upstream 8e20e2019fb4d067e0876fb10e59231dd70c5761, agentRuntimeConfiguration in packages/occ/src/index.ts has no Compute preparation hook. Standard presets enable Control UI without the Agent origin or device approval; tests/integration/native-admin-k3d-real.test.mjs still PATCHes Configuration and redeploys through redeployWithNativeAdminAccess. This demonstrates the remaining first-deployment gap.

Generic refresh concern: upstream packages/occ/src/gateway-security-defaults.ts supplies sandbox, exec and workspace defaults, and commit 08f3658ed injects the Agent display name into the admitted snapshot. First-admin's tests/integration/native-admin-access.test.mjs asserts revision.configuration.agents equals the unmodified preset. That expectation must accommodate upstream behavior while still proving saved Configuration immutability.

Generic refresh concern: upstream commit 7ed3402dd hardens native-admin socket closure and audit ownership; tests/conformance/native-admin-upgrade-reset.test.mjs covers delayed denial audits, shutdown and resets. Preserve these changes in apps/controller/src/http/native-admin.ts; first-admin's actual feature delta there only removes the unused revision argument.

Upstream managed mode remains consequential: tests/integration/native-admin-k3d-real.test.mjs explicitly disables gatewayManagedMode before testing native Configuration writes, then re-enables it and verifies rejection. Automatic first-deployment access must retain that restriction and its test coverage.

Combination adaptation: at roles f30db5c4045cbf2c1f5eef4576361112535ed8b4, Kubernetes runtime-access.ts requires literal coverage of each assigned role's scopes, and index.ts renders managed identities with allowUsers: []. First-admin instead rejects authored allowUsers other than the service identity and enforces exactly [operator.admin] approval scopes. Simply combining these sources rejects supported role policy or leaves limited roles unavailable.

Supported tests include first OpenClaw/Codex deployment, sibling-origin isolation, opt-outs and conflicts in native-admin-access.test.mjs; durable provisioning/replay in postgres-agent-provisioning.test.mjs; and API/worker input parity in development-packaging.test.mjs and production-kubernetes-packaging.test.mjs. The HTTP tests simulate cluster effects; they do not prove installed runtime behavior.

Verification at 37fac70df: node scripts/ci/run-tests.mjs audit passed with no issues; git diff --check passed. node --test tests/integration/native-admin-access.test.mjs failed during module loading because typebox is unavailable, before behavioral tests ran. PostgreSQL, Kubernetes and hosted CI outcomes were not verified. First-admin changes no migration files.
suggestions: Retain the preparation hook at revision admission. Preserve upstream gateway security defaults, Agent-name injection, validation and managed-mode behavior; update the owning first-deployment assertions accordingly. These are ordinary upstream refresh requirements, separate from feature-combination work.

For roles composition, make preparation respect the role-aware transport and device-approval policy while retaining exact runtime assignments, revocation, explicit opt-outs and conflict rejection. Extend existing native-admin tests with first-deployment administrator and limited-role access, unassigned-user denial, and revocation. Do not infer human runtime authority from OCE administration.
Keep shared channel/Secret validation and accepted bound reference forms unchanged. This feature's delta does not establish a Configuration-save regression or justify replacing save rules.

Validate the refreshed candidate through the existing baseline, PostgreSQL provisioning, packaging and gateway-routing lanes when dependencies and infrastructure are available. Preserve upstream socket/audit and managed-mode cases alongside first-deployment coverage.
Keep published migration SQL and journals unchanged. No migration evolution is required by first-admin itself.

order_suggestions.reason: Prefer establishing the role-aware transport contract before adapting automatic preparation. This is composition order only; both source features remain independently useful and must not be restacked.
evidence: roles: apps/controller/src/drivers/compute/kubernetes/runtime-access.ts humanRuntimeAccess checks assigned-role scopes against device approval.
first-admin: apps/controller/src/drivers/compute/kubernetes/native-admin.ts configureNativeAdmin enforces the service-only administrator approval policy.

report.summary: Outbound remains useful and is not absorbed by frozen upstream. Retain its revision-owned egress and durable withdrawal behavior, fix the Configuration-save regression, preserve newer upstream validation, and apply the authorized Teams/embedded adaptations. No intent decision is required. No files or remote state were changed.
evidence: At a50b14647, packages/contracts/src/gateway-outbound.ts defines channelsOnly/restricted/publicHttps selections and immutable requirements. packages/occ/src/index.ts authorizes policy changes with exact-Agent update plus administer and snapshots admission during deployment. Frozen upstream 8e20e2019 has no corresponding GatewayOutbound implementation.

apps/controller/src/drivers/compute/kubernetes/index.ts:14502 reconciles revision-owned proxies and NetworkPolicies, combines admitted and current exclusion CIDRs, and closes existing proxy Pods before replacing changed policy. apps/controller/src/worker.ts persists REVISION_ACCESS_WITHDRAWAL_PENDING before removal and retries across restored authority. Upstream's existing public-GitHub reader withdrawal is narrower and does not replace this feature.

Confirmed generic regression: commit 27562ebf56 introduced the blanket proxy-environment rejection in apps/controller/src/drivers/compute/kubernetes/index.ts:4528. Outbound tests/integration/configuration-controller.test.mjs:1260 expects HTTP_PROXY save rejection and replaces the previous acceptance example with APP_REGION. At frozen upstream, the same owning suite explicitly accepts HTTP_PROXY in Configuration saves (around line 1896).

Upstream replacement to retain: commits c40b22b6f, 56af0a512 and 3918205bc establish shared channel/Secret validation in packages/occ/src/channel-secret-bindings.ts and its Configuration-save callers. Outbound still carries the older recursive collector in Kubernetes Compute. Frozen upstream tests/integration/configuration-controller.test.mjs covers missing bindings, accepted forms, Slack-readable references, and scope to bundled Kubernetes Compute.

Slack refresh requirements: outbound apps/controller/src/drivers/channel/slack.ts:170 accepts only object references. Upstream commit 6c16c2266 also accepts a whole ${NAME}; tests/conformance/slack-channel-directory.test.mjs explicitly covers it. Preserve upstream 07749e5e7's null terminal cursor handling and the newer proxy-availability diagnostics when adding outbound requirement declarations.

Teams composition: outbound apps/controller/src/composition/channel.ts selects Slack alone. Selected Teams source 93c1dc4f supplies BundledChannelDriver in apps/controller/src/drivers/channel/index.ts and serving-Deployment-owned callback reconciliation in Kubernetes Compute. Its directory, callback and guarded-media behavior must survive replacement of the old shared outbound proxy.

Embedded composition: selected source 94346f81 gates channel execution with experimentalEmbeddedChannels. Outbound admitGatewayOutbound and requireChannelTopology currently require dedicated execution; migrations/0064_gateway_outbound.sql also restricts outbound snapshots to dedicated Harnesses. These require the authorized channel-only embedded adaptation, without granting embedded Agents additional restricted/publicHttps authority.

Migration compatibility: previous integration 90e30b8c published migrations/0056_gateway_outbound.sql and 0057_embedded_channel_outbound.sql. Outbound now carries a changed 0064_gateway_outbound.sql, while upstream publishes 0064_gateway_managed_mode.sql. evidence: Verified all refreshed heads against frozen upstream 8e20e2019fb4d067e0876fb10e59231dd70c5761: profiles=89ba3c69e1c8251278cb40971f6166a00f832de6; secrets=b8510e379cfc9ea301406d4092ba05b09ef1126e; plugins=5521c0280c7907dfd38742986f3d3fef5fa92482; roles=489576d57120f1f83da371c0dd5a22bc7c7fddf8; first-admin=a768ca1bf094392d590034c17c5701d0ab549e8f; outbound=56854e0730d8fbf6384012426676e16439cb3022; teams=0a52d37243653170f8924ff1b679bef3239ab695; embedded=94c824071c9b0ae248a4ebb4a22d3e44b5532cfc. Each merge base is the frozen upstream. Conclusions below use these refreshed trees, not the original source heads.

Outbound/Teams: integration compatibility, not an existing source dependency. Outbound adds ChannelDriver.gatewayNetworkRequirements/controlPlaneNetworkRequirements in packages/contracts/src/index.ts:2217 and snapshots requirements through packages/occ/src/index.ts:10443. Its composition/channel.ts constructs only SlackChannelDriver. Teams adds BundledChannelDriver in drivers/channel/index.ts, but that wrapper has neither requirements method. Composition must aggregate both providers through the generic managed transport. Keeping outbound before Teams is a reasonable implementation preference already satisfied by the historical order; reversing them does not eliminate this adaptation.

Outbound/embedded: integration compatibility includes persisted invariants. Outbound KubernetesComputeDriver.admitGatewayOutbound at drivers/compute/kubernetes/index.ts:3240 requires dedicated execution, and migrations/0065_gateway_outbound.sql also rejects outbound snapshots for embedded revisions. Embedded instead enables runtime.channels.experimentalEmbeddedChannels using the older channel proxy configuration. Supporting the requested trial needs coordinated admission, lifecycle, rendering and forward-only database evolution, restricted to channel-derived destinations. Reordering cannot supply that behavior. Outbound conformance tests at tests/conformance/kubernetes-compute.test.mjs:1490 and :1572 cover proxy readiness and withdrawal; embedded tests at :10029 cover trusted opt-in.

Teams/embedded: neither source requires the other to provide its callback implementation. Teams reconcileTeamsRoute at drivers/compute/kubernetes/index.ts:13896 uses the serving Deployment's msteams-webhook annotation; embedded reconcileTeamsCallback at :13897 checks the exact serving revision and manages additional callback Service/NetworkPolicy resources. Their combined implementation must retain serving annotation authority, exact ownership/revision/UID/resourceVersion fencing, provider cutover and complete cleanup. The embedded callback test at tests/conformance/kubernetes-compute.test.mjs:5432 is simulated manifest evidence. Teams tests/integration/runtime-image-startup.test.mjs:726 and tests/fixtures/teams-attachment-download.mjs exercise guarded native media transport. Choosing either merge order does not reconcile these lifecycle differences or preserve the media guards automatically.

Roles/first-admin: integration compatibility, with no demonstrated direction requirement. Roles authorizes exact human/Agent use and returns the configured role through packages/iam/src/index.ts:1203 and packages/occ/src/index.ts:4736. First-admin adds deployment-time Compute.configureAgent and native-admin.ts, whose configureNativeAdmin fixes device approval scopes to operator.admin. Roles runtime-access.ts:159 requires the approval ceiling to include the selected role's actual scopes. These policies must be reconciled without granting runtime use through administration alone. Relevant tests are roles tests/integration/native-admin-access.test.mjs:1516 and first-admin tests/integration/postgres-agent-provisioning.test.mjs:5966. The latter explicitly simulates runtime readiness while exercising HTTP/PostgreSQL/worker handoff. Upstream assigning-session error handling remains present in the roles head at packages/occ/src/state/postgres-state.ts:900.

Profiles/secrets/plugins: inspected implementations do not establish ordering dependencies. Profiles changes trusted profile loading, Preset seeding and starter selection; secrets grants access from accepted saved Configuration bindings in console/agents/create.mts; plugins preserves explicit policy and adds requireHarnessPluginPolicy admission. Their shared editor and test files do not imply direction. Relevant coverage includes profiles 'profile preset selection reaches startup and rolls both controllers', secrets 'Embedded Preset grants all bound Secrets and retries denied access without duplicate writes', and plugins 'Harness switches preserve unrestricted and explicit native plugin allowlists through Agent creation'.

Profile/embedded rendering requires adaptation rather than reordering. Embedded scripts/render-installation-profile.mjs renders the opt-in inside runtime.channels, but accepts legacy runtimeProxyUrl/managedSlackProxy inputs. Its tests/integration/profile-renderer.test.mjs:403–441 check opt-in warnings and matching API/worker checksums. Final composition must preserve those properties while requiring enabled managed outbound and removing legacy proxy configuration. Profiles supplies no missing interface that would justify moving it.

Migration collisions do not establish dependency or direction. Roles and outbound independently append journal index 65 after upstream, modifying different capabilities. Previous integration 90e30b8c6922732ba456ed102b5c72a79fa84b8c has a different 62-entry journal prefix. Final composition must preserve that published SQL/journal history and append evolution; changing feature order cannot resolve this requirement.

Verification was read-only source, interface, SQL and test inspection. Tests and hosted CI were not executed or qualified; no merge simulation was performed. Compatibility findings are not standalone source-defect claims. No files, Git objects, refs or remote state were changed; the checkout remains clean at frozen upstream. No permanent ordering policy is proposed.

feedback: Migration ownership clarification: preservation of all 62 SQL files and journal entries from starting_integration applies to the FINAL COMBINED INTEGRATION only, enforced by the engine preserve guard and integration check. Standalone feature refreshes must remain upstream-contributable: retain frozen upstream migration history and this feature own intentional migration; never import unrelated role/embedded/private integration migrations. Append/adapt the standalone feature migration after upstream as needed and qualify its actual catalog through the required PostgreSQL CI. Keep existing upstream SQL immutable. The current original feature PR remains entirely untouched. Final composition later reconciles feature/upstream evolution onto the old integration 62-entry prefix with forward-only appends. This resolves ownership within the existing authorized intent; no new product behavior or source stack is requested. Do not install or reconcile local dependencies to run checks. Report missing local prerequisites honestly; final canonical CI must supply the actual PostgreSQL, API/browser and native proof.

The current human task is to build/test a separate combined candidate, keeping original PRs/main/integration unchanged. A coding-stage status of completed means that bounded coding work is finished; it never means the whole candidate is qualified. Report actual gaps honestly. Do not use assessment-only needed status for coding. Keep new catalog hashes explicitly null until real measurement; do not invent them or weaken the production guard. The new committed control recipe has an actual PostgreSQL 18.6/Drizzle 0.45.4 fresh/incremental and dump/restore measurement for every prefix; it will measure the FINAL combined SQL, then canonical full CI will prove guarded populated upgrades and application behavior. The older recipe in this parent run has a known inventory bug counting init-local.sql as a migration. Do not delete or change that bootstrap helper or falsify product layout to accommodate the bug: finish clean composition, preserve all 62 SQL/journal entries, and let the operator create a versioned check-policy revalidation run afterward.
Do not invoke local pnpm at all while the matching graph is absent: the disable flag did not prevent automatic reconciliation. Do not install, copy, link or reconcile dependencies. Use direct dependency-independent Node audits/syntax/flow checks; missing local dependencies remain explicit gaps supplied by normal hosted CI later. No Git commits/ref/config edits or remote writes by coding workers.
For final composition, preserve current upstream's CI-owned four native verification jobs (manual ci.yml calls container-check.yml). Do not dispatch a second native workflow. The fork repository Node-base variable remains the older 934... digest and MUST stay unchanged. Source CI currently passes that variable even though checked-in images-packaging/Dockerfile use the new 6449... Node24.22.1 digest. Correct the candidate CI call using a checked-in-source-derived job output, retaining all four native jobs, approved host/AppArmor/archive-import adapters and publication approval gates. The new control check refuses this known stale-base mismatch before candidate publication. This is an integration-only correction, not authority to change image recipes/pins, repository variables or releases.
